newsitem.title: CANADA: 1999 PAN AM GAMES BUDGET QUESTIONED.
newsitem.headline: 1999 PAN AM GAMES BUDGET QUESTIONED.

text.p: As 300 members from the 42 nations of the Pan American Sports Organisation (PASO) gather in Canada for the first time for their annual meeting, questions have arisen about ballooning costs for the 1999 Pan American Games in Winnipeg.

Organisers of the 1999 Games are now looking to the provincial and federal governments for as much as C$40 million ($30 million U.S.) on top of the C$60 million ($45 million U.S.) in government funding already committed towards the C$145 million ($107 million U.S.) project.

The original budget was pegged at C$122 million ($90 million U.S.). Organisers overestimated the value of the Games to advertisers and network broadcasters, resulting in a predicted shortfall in revenues. Also, costs for staging the Games will be higher than first expected.
However, PASO member and Canadian Olympic Association CEO Carol Anne Letheren says everything appears to be "right on track."

"These games are in good shape at this point in time. Compared to all previous games, progress to date has been the best ever. The PASO members will tour the venue sites while in Winnipeg and see the kind of preparations in place. To have the athletes' villages all in place two years out is wonderful.

"The Canadian Olympic Association will go into the PASO assembly here and give a report on the progress that's been made towards the hosting of the 1999 Pan Am Games and this will be the best report that PASO has ever received. Three of the four television network packages are in place and one third of the corporate sector funding is in place."

The Pan Am Games Society has deals with the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation and The Sports Network to broadcast the Games in Canada and with CBU and OTI to broadcast the Games in the Caribbean, Central and South America. Negotiations continue with ABC and ESPN for coverage in the United States.
The Chairman of the Pan Am Games Board says the Canadian, provincial and civic governments meet with organisers regularly to discuss budget issues.

"We have gone through numerous budgets and each time we find out something new about the costs and as costs become more clear, additional requirements are identified and put into the mix," said Chairman Sanford Riley. "We are putting on an extremely prudent games.

"We will do it for between 140 and 145 million dollars (104 and 107 million dollars U.S.). I would like to get it resolved as quickly as possible because we need to make more commitments and we need to start spending on facilities."
The PASO general assembly in Winnipeg, the Manitoba provincial capital at the geographic centre of Canada, will be chaired by PASO President Mario Vazquez Rana of Mexico.

Through Sunday, there will be further discussion of the preparations for the 1999 Pan Am Games in Winnipeg as well as presentations by cities vying to host the 2003 Pan Am Games and the 2004 Summer Olympics.

With 5,000 athletes from 42 countries of North, South, Central America and the Caribbean participating in 41 sports, the 1999 Pan Am Games will be the third largest competition ever held in North America, eclipsed only by the Summer Olympics in Los Angeles and Atlanta. Winnipeg also hosted the Pan Am Games in 1967.
